2027-01-14.title: Thursday of the First Week in Ordinary Time
readings: Today, if you hear his voice
If today you hear his voice, harden not your hearts
Moved with pity, Jesus touched him
2027-01-14.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 1 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green. In India: St Devasahayam, martyr (check the diocesan calendar).
2027-01-14.verse: Moved with pity, Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him, and said to him, “I do choose. Be made clean!”
theo: Hebrews takes up Psalm 95: “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion.” The generation in the wilderness saw God's works for forty years and still hardened their hearts. The warning is urgent: “exhort one another every day, as long as it is called ‘today,’ so that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.” Faith is kept alive day by day, and we are responsible for one another.

In Mark a leper comes to Jesus and kneels: “If you choose, you can make me clean.” Mark notes that Jesus was “moved with pity”, a word for a compassion felt in the depths of the body. He touches the man and heals him. Then a striking reversal: the healed man spreads the news, and Jesus “could no longer go into a town openly, but stayed out in the country.” The leper comes back into town, and Jesus takes his place outside. In India today many remember St Devasahayam, a court official who embraced Christ and, rejecting caste barriers, mixed freely with people of every community; arrested for his faith, he was executed in 1752. He too went outside the camp with Jesus.
outline: Ask: when did compassion move you to act?
The healed man returns; Jesus stays outside.
live: Send a message of faith and encouragement to someone struggling.
Spend time with someone others exclude, as Jesus and St Devasahayam did.
2027-01-14.prayer: Lord Jesus, moved with pity you touched the leper and took his place outside. Today let me hear your voice and not harden my heart. Through the prayers of St Devasahayam, give me courage to love across every barrier. Amen.
altar: Hebrews says Jesus suffered outside the city gate (Hebrews 13:12). At the altar we meet the One who went outside for us.

quick: Today, do not harden your hearts.

2027-01-14.question: Is my heart soft or hard toward God's voice today?

family.explain: A man with a skin disease begged Jesus for help. Jesus felt sorry for him, touched him and healed him.
family.intention: We pray for people who are left out by others.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone at school or work who is left alone? How can we be kind?”

illus: St Devasahayam (Neelakanta Pillai) was a respected official in eighteenth-century Travancore. After his Baptism he refused to treat anyone as untouchable and shared meals with people of every caste. This scandalised many. He accepted imprisonment and death rather than deny Christ. Pope Francis canonised him in 2022, the first Indian layman to be declared a saint.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, today we hear your voice. Soften our hearts, and move us with your pity for the suffering. Amen.
share: Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts (Hebrews 3:7–8). Where is my heart hard?
Exhort one another every day (Hebrews 3:13). Whom can I encourage today?
Moved with pity, Jesus touched him (Mark 1:41). Whom am I afraid to touch?
interc: For people with leprosy and all who are excluded.
For Christians in India, through the prayers of St Devasahayam.
For those who have hardened their hearts against God.
For those who encourage others in faith.
For our group, that we may encourage one another daily.
pm.close: Father, your Son was moved with pity and touched the outcast. Keep our hearts soft to your voice, and give us his compassion for all. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews quotes Psalm 95 with great urgency: today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts (Hebrews 3:7–8). The people in the wilderness saw God's works for forty years and still turned away. A heart can harden slowly, without noticing.

The remedy is community: exhort one another every day, as long as it is called today, so that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin (Hebrews 3:13). We need each other to stay soft toward God.

In the Gospel a leper kneels before Jesus: if you choose, you can make me clean. Mark says Jesus was moved with pity, a compassion felt deep inside. He stretched out his hand and touched him: I do choose. Be made clean! (Mark 1:41).

Then something surprising happens. The healed man tells everyone, and Jesus could no longer go into a town openly, but stayed out in the country (Mark 1:45). The leper goes back into society; Jesus takes his place outside. That is what Jesus does for us all the way to the Cross.

In India today many honour St Devasahayam, who after his Baptism refused to treat anyone as untouchable and gave his life for Christ. Let us hear the Lord's voice today, keep our hearts soft, and love across every barrier. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus felt so sorry for the sick man that he touched him and made him well. Let us be kind to anyone who is left out.

intro: Theme: “Moved with pity, Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him.”
Today's call, the compassion of Jesus, and the One who goes outside for us.

q: Do not harden your hearts, as at Meribah, as on the day at Massah in the wilderness,
But exhort one another every day, as long as it is called “today,” so that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
points.apply: Encourage one person in faith today.

q: The person who has the leprous disease shall wear torn clothes and let the hair of his head be disheveled; and he shall cover his upper lip and cry out, “Unclean, unclean.”
Moved with pity, Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him, and said to him, “I do choose. Be made clean!”
points.apply: Visit someone who is lonely or excluded.

sub: The healed man spreads the news.
q: But he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the punishment that made us whole, and by his bruises we are healed.
But he went out and began to proclaim it freely, and to spread the word, so that Jesus could no longer go into a town openly, but stayed out in the country; and people came to him from every quarter.
points.apply: Thank Jesus for taking your place.

concl: Today is the day to hear his voice.
Jesus goes outside so that the outcast may come in.
2027-01-14.resolve: Cross one barrier of caste, class or prejudice this week.
